course.title: Interactive Early Science: Animals & Nature
course.description: An engaging, picture-assisted natural science course designed for all learners.

lessons.title: 1. Mammals and Their Habitats
lessons.description: Discover warm-blooded animals and how they adapt to nature.
lessons.content:
### What is a Mammal?

Mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates that have hair or fur, and nourish their young with milk.

![Red Fox in Nature](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1474511320723-9a56873867b5?w=800&auto=format&fit=crop&q=60 "A red fox exploring its natural woodland habitat")

#### Key Characteristics of Mammals:
- They breathe oxygen with lungs.
- They have specialized teeth adapted to their diet.
- Most give birth to live young.

From forest foxes to ocean blue whales, mammals live in almost every climate on Earth!

lessons.title: 2. Birds and the Science of Flight
lessons.description: How feathers and light bones enable birds to soar across the sky.
lessons.content:
### The Marvel of Avian Flight

Birds are feathered, winged animals with exceptional vision and lightweight skeletal systems.

![Bald Eagle Soaring](https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1544383835-bda2bc66a55d?w=800&auto=format&fit=crop&q=60 "An eagle in flight demonstrating wing aerodynamic lift")

#### Adaptations for Flight:
1. Hollow, air-filled bones that reduce body mass.
2. Powerful chest muscles attached to a specialized keel bone.
3. Aerodynamic flight feathers creating high lift with minimal drag.
